name: Afghanistan
fact: The Minaret of Jam is a 65-metre brick tower standing in a deep mountain river valley.

name: Albania
fact: Butrint preserves layers of an ancient Greek colony and a later Roman city at the same site.

name: Algeria
fact: Tassili n'Ajjer has thousands of prehistoric rock pictures among sandstone formations shaped like a stone forest.

name: Andorra
fact: The Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley preserves stone shepherd huts and mountain paths high in the Pyrenees.

name: Angola
fact: Mbanza Kongo stands on a plateau and was the royal capital of the historic Kingdom of Kongo.

name: Antigua and Barbuda
fact: Antigua's naval dockyard was built beside deep, narrow bays that sheltered and helped repair sailing ships.

name: Argentina
fact: In Los Glaciares National Park, huge glaciers end in lakes and break off floating icebergs.

name: Armenia
fact: Several churches and tombs at Geghard monastery were carved directly into the surrounding rock.

name: Australia
fact: The Great Barrier Reef is an enormous coral reef ecosystem off the country's north-east coast.

name: Austria
fact: People were mining salt around Hallstatt thousands of years ago; salt helped the town become prosperous.

name: Azerbaijan
fact: Gobustan has more than 6,000 rock engravings showing traces of people across thousands of years.

name: Bahamas
fact: Dean's Blue Hole on Long Island is a deep underwater sinkhole beside a white-sand beach.

name: Bahrain
fact: An ancient fort called Qal'at stands on a mound built up by many layers of earlier human settlements.

name: Bangladesh
fact: Bengal tigers live in the Sundarbans, a mangrove forest threaded by tidal waterways.

name: Barbados
fact: Old Bridgetown has winding streets, unlike the straight grid used by many other Caribbean colonial towns.

name: Belarus
fact: Mir Castle combines Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque styles because it was rebuilt and extended over centuries.

name: Belgium
fact: The Grand-Place in Brussels is a historic square ringed by ornate public buildings and guild houses.

name: Belize
fact: The coastal reef reserve includes coral reefs, sand islands and mangroves that shelter turtles and manatees.

name: Benin
fact: At Abomey, generations of kings built their royal palaces inside a shared earthen-walled area.

name: Bhutan
fact: Paro Taktsang, nicknamed Tiger's Nest, is a monastery built on a steep cliff above the Paro valley.

name: Bolivia
fact: Salar de Uyuni is a vast salt flat left behind by ancient lakes high in the Andes.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
fact: Mostar is named after its famous Old Bridge, which crosses the Neretva River and was rebuilt after war.

name: Botswana
fact: The Okavango Delta spreads inland instead of reaching the sea, and its flood arrives during the dry season.

name: Brazil
fact: The planned capital Brasilia has a layout often compared to a bird with its wings spread.

name: Brunei
fact: Kampong Ayer is a water settlement where many houses stand on stilts above the river.

name: Bulgaria
fact: Rila Monastery began in the tenth century and was rebuilt after a major fire in the nineteenth century.

name: Burkina Faso
fact: Loropeni's tall stone walls are the remains of a fortress connected with historic gold trading.

name: Burundi
fact: This country shares Lake Tanganyika with Tanzania, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

name: Cabo Verde
fact: Cidade Velha on Santiago Island preserves old streets and a hilltop royal fortress from its port-town past.

name: Cambodia
fact: Angkor Wat is part of a huge archaeological landscape containing former capitals of the Khmer Empire.

name: Cameroon
fact: The Dja River almost completely surrounds Dja Faunal Reserve, forming a natural rainforest boundary.

name: Canada
fact: Dinosaur Provincial Park in Alberta preserves dinosaur fossils about 75 million years old.

name: Central African Republic
fact: Manovo-Gounda St Floris National Park combines broad savannahs with northern floodplains used by water birds.

name: Chad
fact: Wind and water carved the Ennedi sandstone into natural arches, cliffs and canyons in the Sahara.

name: Chile
fact: Rapa Nui, also called Easter Island, is famous for the enormous carved stone figures called moai.

name: China
fact: The Great Wall joined and extended older defensive walls over many centuries.

name: Colombia
fact: In the coffee-growing landscape, farmers grow coffee on small plots along steep Andean mountain slopes.

name: Comoros
fact: Karthala is a volcano on Grande Comore with a summit caldera several kilometres across.

name: Congo (Republic)
fact: Congo shares the Sangha Trinational forest site with Cameroon and the Central African Republic.

name: Costa Rica
fact: Cocos Island has tropical rainforest above water and ocean habitats visited by sharks, rays and dolphins below.

name: Croatia
fact: At Plitvice Lakes, flowing water deposits mineral barriers that form natural dams, lakes and waterfalls.

name: Cuba
fact: The old city of Trinidad preserves grand houses built during its eighteenth- and nineteenth-century sugar-trading era.

name: Cyprus
fact: Ancient Paphos preserves Roman-era villas with detailed mosaic floors.

name: Czechia
fact: Kutna Hora grew wealthy from silver mines, helping pay for its remarkable Gothic church of St Barbara.

name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
fact: Virunga National Park includes mountain-gorilla habitat, volcano slopes and even high mountain snowfields.

name: Denmark
fact: Kronborg Castle is known as Elsinore, the setting of Shakespeare's play Hamlet.

name: Djibouti
fact: Lake Assal is an extremely salty lake whose surface lies about 155 metres below sea level.

name: Dominica
fact: Morne Trois Pitons National Park contains hot springs, volcanoes and a steaming feature named Boiling Lake.

name: Dominican Republic
fact: Santo Domingo's old town used a street grid that became a model for later colonial towns in the Americas.

name: Ecuador
fact: The Galapagos Islands' giant tortoises and unusual finches helped inspire Charles Darwin's ideas about evolution.

name: Egypt
fact: The pyramid fields around ancient Memphis include the giant royal tombs at Giza.

name: El Salvador
fact: Joya de Ceren is a farming village preserved beneath volcanic ash from an eruption around AD 600.

name: Equatorial Guinea
fact: On Bioko Island, lowland rainforest gives way to mountain forests as the land rises.

name: Eritrea
fact: Asmara sits more than 2,000 metres above sea level and is known for its early modernist buildings.

name: Estonia
fact: Tallinn's old town preserves medieval merchants' houses from its days in the Hanseatic trading network.

name: Eswatini
fact: Sibebe Rock near Mbabane is a huge exposed granite dome that walkers can climb.

name: Ethiopia
fact: Lalibela has eleven medieval churches hewn from solid rock rather than assembled from separate stone blocks.

name: Fiji
fact: Levuka, the country's first colonial capital, is a waterfront town with low buildings among coconut and mango trees.

name: Finland
fact: Suomenlinna is a sea fortress built across a group of islands at the entrance to Helsinki's harbour.

name: France
fact: Mont-Saint-Michel is an abbey and village on a rocky islet surrounded by sandbanks and strong tides.

name: Gabon
fact: Lope-Okanda brings dense rainforest and ancient savannah together in the same protected landscape.

name: Gambia
fact: Wassu's ancient stone circles are part of the Senegambian landscape of upright stone pillars and burial mounds.

name: Georgia
fact: Upper Svaneti has mountain villages with stone tower-houses once used as both homes and defensive shelters.

name: Germany
fact: Cologne Cathedral was started in 1248 but was not completed until 1880, more than six centuries later.

name: Ghana
fact: The coast preserves stone forts and castles built as trading posts between the fifteenth and eighteenth centuries.

name: Greece
fact: The Parthenon stands on the Acropolis, the rocky hill above Athens with ancient temples and monuments.
